narrative.northStar: Editorial Beauty — the Booking Is the Cover.
narrative.overview: NAP is a beauty booking surface designed like a fashion editorial. The appointment is the look; each booking reads as a cover story, not a service menu. The system rejects the soft-pink beauty default in favor of a near-black studio backdrop, bone-white paper, and one flat unmissable block of signal red. Display type is monumental and behaves like matter — the hero word BOOKED fragments the bottom of its own letters as it settles into place. Everything else holds deliberate negative space; sections are paced like magazine spreads rather than product pages. Personality: warm, confident, lightly playful — never cutesy, never clinical. Density: low. Ornament: zero. The signal red, the hairline, and the monumental type do all the talking; nothing else competes.
keyCharacteristics: Two-tone canvas (bone paper + ink studio) with one flat signal accent
Sharp corners everywhere (4px); hairlines (1px) carry all division
Mono micro-labels set at 11px with 0.18em tracking act as the system's 'stage directions'
Spectral italic is reserved for the editorial whisper line ('with your artist', 'Booked with your artist.')
Display type is monumental (up to 156px), tight (-0.04em tracking), and animated like physical matter
Glow appears exactly once: a soft red bloom under the primary CTA

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is used on roughly one element per fold. Hover tints do not exist; saturation is held at one register so the CTA always reads first.

rules.name: The Two-Canvas Rule
rules.body: The page alternates between Bone and Ink. Bone carries commercial intent (hero, artists, FAQ); Ink carries system intent (how-it-works, footer). Never split a single section across both.

rules.name: The Whisper Rule
rules.body: Spectral italic is reserved for the editorial subtitle that follows a Display or Headline. It is never used for body, navigation, or supporting copy. Its scarcity is what gives it warmth.

rules.name: The Tight-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline track tight (-0.04em / -0.035em). Mono tracks open (+0.18em). The two regimes never bleed into each other; one is sculpture, the other is measurement.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Depth appears only as a response to state (hover, focus) and only on the primary CTA. Hairlines and Ink-on-Bone contrast carry all other separation.

dos: Use Signal Red sparingly — one element per fold. Each new use must displace an existing use, not add.
Set body text on contrast verified at AA against its surface (ink on bone, bone on ink).
Preserve --space-9 and --space-10 as section paddings. Sections that feel cramped have lost the negative-space doctrine.
Use mono micro-labels for any metadata, table column, caption, or step numeral.
Inline an SVG arrow on CTAs and any other 'go forward' gesture. Never use Unicode arrows.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion — the BOOKED fragment settles instantly, the CTA bloom stays static, smooth scrolling is disabled.
donts: Introduce a second accent color. There is one voice; it speaks through Signal Red.
Add an eyebrow / kicker label above a heading. This house refuses kickers; reintroducing one is a craft violation.
Soften corners beyond 4px or round individual elements differently from the system default.
Decorate with icon fonts, glyph icons, or Lucide-style outline icons. Ink lines and SVG arrows are the only marks allowed.
Ship a section without an aria-label or aria-labelledby. Landmarks and headings carry the page for screen readers.
Invent testimonials, reviews, or artist names. All copy and imagery on this surface is placeholder by intent — replace before any go-live.
Reuse the hero BOOKED animation on any other element. The fragment is reserved for the first viewport and earns its drama by being singular.
